component.name: Qtmonitor
component.summary: Resource and task monitor for Linux

description.p: A Qt6/KF6 resource and task monitor with the clear, at-a-glance layout Windows Task Manager is known for, delivered as a Linux-native tool. It runs correctly on any desktop environment or window manager, and needs no monitoring daemon.

ul.li: A live process table fed from /proc, with configurable columns that persist between runs, search, and a kernel-thread toggle
CPU usage as a share of total capacity, the way Task Manager reports it, rather than per-core percentages that exceed 100
Ending a process sends SIGTERM and then offers SIGKILL, using real signal names; another user's process raises polkit's own authentication dialog
Per-resource pages for CPU, memory, every GPU, every disk and every network interface, each with live graphs painted from the desktop's own palette
Disk active time charted separately from throughput, because a disk can be saturated at a low transfer rate
XDG autostart entries and systemd user units listed together in one Startup Apps tab, each enableable in place
Per-user session summaries from logind, with that user's processes one expand away
Values that genuinely cannot be read show an em dash rather than a misleading zero

description.p: AMD and Intel GPUs are read straight from sysfs and DRM fdinfo with no extra tool. NVIDIA cards need nvidia-utils, since the proprietary driver publishes neither; a card without it still gets a page explaining why its graphs are empty.
